Discussion In contrast to our first hypothesis, this study shows that athletes were able to consume amounts of carbohydrates which were in accordance with the current recommen- dations for longer events [6,7]. However, despite of this fact, these athletes did not meet their energy require- ments during the event resulting in a higher energy defi- cit. Thus, these results confirmed partially our preliminary hypotheses and were in agreement with two previous investigations showing that, like solo events, a high energy deficit is common in a team relay format events despite that athletes have considerable time to recover between bouts of exercise [4,26]. One explana- tion for this effect has been related with appetite sup- pression since it is known that longer exercise induces a suppression of acylated ghrelin in humans [27].
